title: Mitigate queue-starvation and extreme long-context tail latency in scheduler
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Multiple customers reported production regressions: intermittent request starvation for short requests and extreme P99.9 tail latency for very long-context generations. Incidents observed across Hosted and Dedicated customers and a private deployment. This ticket tracked triage, patch implementation, and rollout of a scheduler and batching runtime fix to eliminate starvation and reduce long-context tail latencies.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy runtime-1.23 with continuous-batching enabled (default config).
2) Start mixed workload: 60% short (<=128 tokens) QPS, 40% long-context (>=32k tokens) persistent generation sessions, sustained for 20+ minutes.
3) Observe per-worker queue depth using /internal/queue_metrics and P99.9 generation latency from tracing.
4) Trigger backpressure by reducing available worker concurrency (simulate spike or capacity drain).

5) Repro shows some short requests stuck behind long sessions or not getting scheduled for multiple batching windows -> starvation; also P99.9 for long contexts spikes due to KV eviction and repeated re-computation of prefixes.
impact_summary: Observed customer errors (4xx timeouts) and amplified tail latency causing failed SLAs. Top impacted customers: NovaHealth (Hosted), LedgerPay (Dedicated), and a private on-prem deployment at FinLedger. Estimated customer request drops: ~2.3% of requests during peak incident windows, with sustained P99.9 latency increases up to 4x on long-context jobs.
root_cause: Combination of scheduler incentives and a subtle race in the continuous-batching scheduler: the token-budget based batching heuristic favored long-context sessions because they claimed large token reservations early, which prevented short requests from being included in batches (starvation). Additionally, a KV cache compaction path triggered while long sessions were actively appending to KV, causing repeated cache misses and rehydration work that multiplied tail latency. A rare dequeuing race led to worker-side queue_depth clamps being set to zero for short-lived queues under backpressure.
proposed_fix: 1) Introduce per-request aging and slot priority: short requests gain priority after a configurable aging threshold to prevent starvation. 2) Token-reservation smoothing: limit early large token reservations to a percentage of a worker's batching window. 3) KV cache compaction guard: block compaction during active prefix append; enable incremental compaction with rate-limiting. 4) Fix dequeuing race by switching to atomic compare-and-swap path and adding unit tests around concurrent enqueue/dequeue. 5) Add e2e long-context harness in CI to detect regressions.
rollback_plan: Roll back scheduler changes via feature-flag (scheduler_v2=false) and revert runtime image to runtime-1.23 if needed. For Dedicated customers we can flip tenant-level flags; for Hosted customers we will perform staged rollback by region. Keep capacity buffer as short-term mitigation while rollback completes.
rollout_plan: Canary: deploy to us-west-2 on 3 small workers (10% of capacity) for 2h with synthetic mixed workload
Gradual ramp: if canary stable, expand to 30% capacity across two regions over 6h
Full rollout: remaining regions after 24h stability and no alert triggers
Dedicated: provision canary pool per customer and coordinate maintenance window with enterprise contacts
Private: ship patch and provide upgrade instructions; QA on customer infra required before enabling scheduler_v2
qa_steps: Unit tests covering enqueue/dequeue race scenarios (added 6 tests).
Integration: long-context e2e harness that reproduces P99.9 regression locally and in staging.
Load tests: mixed short/long workloads at 1.5x production QPS for 30 minutes.
Canary verification checklist: no increase in starved_request_count, P99.9 tail latency within 1.2x baseline, KV compaction rate under threshold.
attachments: PR-2203: runtime scheduler fixes and KV compaction guard

postmortem_summary: Root cause was an interaction between token-reservation heuristics, KV compaction timing, and a rare dequeue race. Quick mitigations (token cap and tenant flags) reduced customer impact immediately. Permanent fixes (aging priority, compaction guard, atomic dequeue) eliminated starvation and restored P99.9 latency to acceptable levels. Action items: add long-context tests to CI, expose starved_queue metric in Console, and schedule a Q2 spike for a fairness-first scheduler redesign.
